description: Benchmark for a local RAG agent over three dynamic-scene reconstruction papers. This version separates method mentions from evidence documents, adds precise evidence locations, distinguishes answerability states, separates summary/retrieval/table/behavior/web groups, and avoids penalizing valid tool strategies.

corpus_manifest.title: Shape of Motion: 4D Reconstruction from a Single Video
MoSca: Dynamic Gaussian Fusion from Casual Videos via 4D Motion Scaffolds
SplineGS: Robust Motion-Adaptive Spline for Real-Time Dynamic 3D Gaussians from Monocular Video

answerability_labels.answerable: The requested fact can be supported by the indexed corpus.
answerability_labels.not_reported: The correct response is that the requested detail is not reported in the indexed corpus.
answerability_labels.external_required: The question requires up-to-date information outside the indexed corpus.
answerability_labels.invalid_document: The requested document is not indexed.

evaluation_notes.retrieval: Evaluate evidence retrieval against required_evidence_documents and evidence locations, not against every method mentioned in the question.
evaluation_notes.summary: Evaluate factual coverage and faithfulness. Do not require a specific internal retrieval sequence if the summary tool can answer correctly.
evaluation_notes.table_questions: Report separately from narrative retrieval because PDF table extraction may separate method names, headers, and values.
evaluation_notes.web_questions: Exclude from the current main score if the agent has no web-search tool. They can instead test whether the agent explicitly acknowledges the capability limit.
evaluation_notes.reference_answers: Keep answers and evidence annotations only in the evaluator. Index only the source PDFs. Send only the question to the evaluated system; corpus identity information may be provided independently of question labels.

retrieval_scoring.evidence_groups: Every question has required evidence groups. Any one page in a group's any_of list covers that group; all groups must be covered for complete evidence coverage. The evidence array supplies human-readable annotations and is not itself a list of mandatory pages.
retrieval_scoring.ranking: K refers to the first K ranked chunks. Deduplicate filename/page pairs within that prefix for coverage; do not compress ranks or fetch extra chunks to obtain K unique pages.
retrieval_scoring.page_hit_at_k: 1 if any required group is covered by the first K chunks, otherwise 0.
retrieval_scoring.page_recall_at_k: Number of covered required evidence groups divided by the total number of required evidence groups. Alternative pages count as one group, and repeated chunks from a page do not add coverage.
retrieval_scoring.page_mrr_at_k: Mean of per-question reciprocal ranks. Use the original chunk rank of the first result matching any required group, or 0 if no match occurs in the first K chunks.
retrieval_scoring.complete_evidence_at_k: 1 only if all required groups are covered in the first K chunks, otherwise 0. Report this alongside hit and MRR for comparisons.
retrieval_scoring.aggregation: Macro-average over eligible questions; also report narrative_retrieval and table_quantitative separately. Include Q27 in the narrative report.
retrieval_scoring.limitation: Page matches are a coarse proxy for evidence retrieval. They do not establish that the retrieved chunk contains the answer. Save retrieved text for manual inspection; passage-level scores require supporting spans or excerpts.

reproducibility.missing_metadata_policy: Record unavailable model revisions explicitly as unknown; do not infer them.
reproducibility.artifact_policy: Save per-question ranked chunks with original rank, filename, page, chunk ID, score, and text alongside aggregate scores.

questions.question: Summarize the main problem, core idea, and key contributions of Shape of Motion.
questions.reference_answer: Shape of Motion addresses monocular 4D reconstruction of dynamic scenes. It represents the scene with persistent 3D Gaussians and models their motion using a compact set of shared SE(3) motion bases, so each Gaussian follows a long-range 3D trajectory in world coordinates. It consolidates noisy monocular depth and long-range 2D tracking priors into a globally consistent 4D representation, enabling long-range 2D/3D tracking and novel-view synthesis.

evidence.supports: Problem, SE(3) motion bases, monocular depth and 2D-track priors, state-of-the-art claims.
Persistent 3D Gaussians, long-range trajectories, two key contributions.

questions.question: Summarize the main problem, core representation, and reconstruction pipeline of MoSca.
questions.reference_answer: MoSca targets fully automatic 4D reconstruction and novel-view synthesis from casual monocular videos, including pose-free inputs. It represents deformation with a sparse 4D Motion Scaffold whose graph nodes are 6-DoF trajectories and whose motions are smoothly interpolated to dense scene points. The system obtains depth, long-term tracks, and motion cues from foundation models, estimates camera parameters, optimizes the scaffold with physical regularization, and globally fuses dynamic 3D Gaussians across time for rendering.

evidence.supports: Pose-free monocular reconstruction, Motion Scaffold, foundation-model priors, Gaussian fusion.
Sparse graph nodes, 6-DoF trajectories, interpolation of dense deformation.

questions.question: Summarize the main idea of SplineGS and explain the roles of MAS and MACP.
questions.reference_answer: SplineGS is a COLMAP-free dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting framework for monocular videos. Motion-Adaptive Spline (MAS) represents each dynamic Gaussian trajectory with piecewise cubic Hermite splines. Motion-Adaptive Control Points Pruning (MACP) adapts trajectory complexity by pruning unnecessary control points while preserving more control points for complex motion. SplineGS also jointly optimizes camera parameters and Gaussian attributes.

evidence.supports: COLMAP-free framework, MAS, MACP, joint camera/Gaussian optimization.
Two-stage optimization and MAS/MACP overview.

questions.question: What off-the-shelf priors does Shape of Motion use, and why are they useful?
questions.reference_answer: Shape of Motion uses monocular depth estimates and long-range 2D point tracks. Depth provides per-frame geometric cues, while long-range tracks provide correspondence and motion cues. The method consolidates these noisy complementary priors into a globally coherent representation of scene geometry and motion.

evidence.supports: Monocular depth and long-range 2D tracks are explicitly named as priors.
The rendered RGB, depth, and tracks are compared with input signals to supervise the representation.

questions.question: How is a MoSca graph node defined, and how is a dense SE(3) deformation obtained from the sparse graph?
questions.reference_answer: Each MoSca node stores a 6-DoF trajectory represented by per-timestep SE(3) rigid transformations plus a control radius. Nodes are connected with a KNN topology using a curve-distance metric. For a query point, nearby node motions are weighted by radial-basis-function skinning weights and blended with Dual Quaternion Blending, which produces an interpolated SE(3) transform.

evidence.supports: Node definition, graph topology, RBF weights, and Dual Quaternion Blending.

questions.question: Why does SplineGS use cubic Hermite splines instead of a fixed-degree polynomial trajectory model?
questions.reference_answer: SplineGS argues that fixed-degree polynomial trajectories have limited flexibility when motion complexity varies. Piecewise cubic Hermite splines can adapt local trajectory shape through control points, while MACP adjusts how many control points are needed. In the ablation, both third- and tenth-degree polynomial variants have worse rendering quality than MAS, and the tenth-degree polynomial is described as numerically unstable.

evidence.supports: Fixed-degree polynomial trajectories are described as inflexible for complex motion.
Polynomial ablation and numerical-instability discussion.

questions.question: Compare how Shape of Motion, MoSca, and SplineGS handle camera parameters.
questions.reference_answer: Shape of Motion takes camera intrinsics and world-to-camera extrinsics as inputs. For in-the-wild videos, it initializes camera poses using MegaSaM and refines them during optimization; for public benchmarks, it uses dataset-provided camera annotations. MoSca is designed for pose-free monocular videos and estimates focal length and camera poses using bundle adjustment followed by photometric refinement. SplineGS is also COLMAP-free: it first performs a warm-up camera-parameter optimization with photometric and geometric consistency, then jointly optimizes camera parameters and 3D Gaussians during main training.

evidence.supports: Camera intrinsics and world-to-camera extrinsics are listed as inputs.
MegaSaM initialization and pose refinement apply to in-the-wild videos; public benchmarks use dataset-provided camera annotations.
Bundle adjustment and photometric optimization for focal length and poses.
Warm-up and main-stage camera optimization.

questions.question: Compare the motion representations used by Shape of Motion, MoSca, and SplineGS.
questions.reference_answer: Shape of Motion uses a compact global set of shared SE(3) motion bases, with each Gaussian assigned coefficients over those bases. MoSca uses a sparse structured graph of 6-DoF trajectory nodes and interpolates nearby node transforms to obtain dense deformation. SplineGS models each dynamic Gaussian trajectory directly with a cubic Hermite spline whose number of control points is adapted by MACP.

evidence.supports: Shared SE(3) bases and per-Gaussian motion coefficients.
Sparse trajectory graph and interpolated deformation field.
Per-Gaussian cubic Hermite spline and MACP.

questions.question: How do Shape of Motion and MoSca differ in the way they impose low-dimensional structure on scene motion?
questions.reference_answer: Shape of Motion uses a compact shared set of SE(3) motion bases and expresses each point or Gaussian motion as a weighted combination of those bases. MoSca instead uses a sparse graph of explicit 6-DoF node trajectories and obtains dense deformation by spatially blending nearby node motions. Both reduce the motion solution space, but one is basis-combination based and the other is sparse trajectory-graph based.

evidence.supports: Compact set of SE(3) motion bases and linear combination.
Sparse graph trajectory representation.

questions.question: Both MoSca and SplineGS are COLMAP-free. What is the main difference in how they obtain camera parameters?
questions.reference_answer: MoSca estimates focal length and camera poses using bundle adjustment followed by photometric refinement. SplineGS uses a warm-up stage that optimizes camera parameters with photometric and geometric consistency, then jointly optimizes the camera and Gaussian representation during main training.
questions.answer_scoring_note: Score the conceptual contrast between the two camera-estimation pipelines. Detailed formulas and the static-tracklet implementation detail are not required.

evidence.supports: Bundle adjustment and photometric optimization.
Warm-up camera estimation and joint main-stage optimization.

questions.question: On the iPhone dataset, how much lower is Shape of Motion's 3D tracking EPE than TAPIR + Depth Anything?
questions.reference_answer: Shape of Motion has EPE 0.082, while TAPIR + Depth Anything has EPE 0.114. The absolute reduction is 0.032, which is about a 28.1% relative reduction compared with TAPIR + Depth Anything.

evidence.supports: TAPIR + DA EPE = 0.114; Shape of Motion EPE = 0.082.

questions.question: On the iPhone dataset, by how many percentage points does Shape of Motion improve 2D tracking AJ over SpatialTracker in world coordinates?
questions.reference_answer: Shape of Motion reports AJ = 34.4, while SpatialTracker in world coordinates reports AJ = 24.9. The improvement is 9.5 percentage points.

evidence.supports: SpatialTracker (world) AJ = 24.9; Shape of Motion AJ = 34.4.

questions.question: On Kubric MOVi-F, how much does Shape of Motion improve delta_3D^0.10 accuracy over CoTracker + Depth Anything?
questions.reference_answer: Shape of Motion reports delta_3D^0.10 = 62.2, compared with 56.5 for CoTracker + Depth Anything. The improvement is 5.7 percentage points.

evidence.supports: CoTracker + DA delta_3D^0.10 = 56.5; Shape of Motion = 62.2.

questions.question: According to the Shape of Motion ablation, what happens to 3D tracking when 2D track supervision is removed?
questions.reference_answer: Removing 2D track supervision increases EPE from 0.082 to 0.141, an absolute degradation of 0.059. delta_3D^0.05 drops from 43.0 to 30.4, and delta_3D^0.10 drops from 73.3 to 57.8, decreases of 12.6 and 15.5 percentage points respectively.

evidence.supports: Full model versus removal of 2D track supervision.

questions.question: Under the DyCheck w-pose setting reported by MoSca, how much does MoSca outperform Shape of Motion in mPSNR and mLPIPS?
questions.reference_answer: MoSca reports 19.32 mPSNR and 0.264 mLPIPS, while Shape of Motion reports 17.32 mPSNR and 0.296 mLPIPS. MoSca is higher by 2.00 dB in mPSNR and lower by 0.032 in mLPIPS.

evidence.supports: Both the MoSca and Shape of Motion DyCheck w-pose rows are present in the same table.

questions.question: Under MoSca's pose-free DyCheck setting, how much better is MoSca than Gaussian Marbles in mPSNR and mLPIPS?
questions.reference_answer: MoSca reports 18.84 mPSNR and 0.289 mLPIPS, while Gaussian Marbles reports 15.79 mPSNR and 0.430 mLPIPS. MoSca improves mPSNR by 3.05 dB and reduces mLPIPS by 0.141.

evidence.supports: Pose-free DyCheck comparison.

questions.question: How much does MoSca improve PCK-T over the raw BootsTAPIR tracker on DyCheck?
questions.reference_answer: MoSca reports PCK-T = 0.824, while BootsTAPIR reports 0.779. The absolute improvement is 0.045, or 4.5 percentage points.

evidence.supports: PCK-T values for BootsTAPIR and MoSca.

questions.question: What is the effect of removing the tracking loss L_track in MoSca?
questions.reference_answer: The paper reports that PCK-T decreases from 0.824 to 0.737 when L_track is removed. That is an absolute drop of 0.087, or 8.7 percentage points.

evidence.supports: PCK-T changes from 0.824 to 0.737 without L_track.

questions.question: Which MoSca ablation causes the largest rendering-quality collapse in Table 5, and by how much does mPSNR change relative to the full model?
questions.reference_answer: Removing the photometric optimization stage causes the largest collapse. mPSNR drops from 19.32 for the full model to 13.71, a decrease of 5.61 dB. mLPIPS also worsens from 0.264 to 0.763.

evidence.supports: Full model and component-ablation metrics.

questions.question: In SplineGS Table 1 on the NVIDIA dataset, how much does SplineGS improve average PSNR and LPIPS over the pose-free MoSca result?
questions.reference_answer: SplineGS reports 27.21 PSNR and 0.053 LPIPS, while the pose-free MoSca row reports 26.61 PSNR and 0.069 LPIPS. SplineGS improves PSNR by 0.60 dB and reduces LPIPS by 0.016.

evidence.supports: Both pose-free MoSca and SplineGS rows are present.

questions.question: Using the FPS values in SplineGS Table 1, approximately how many times faster is SplineGS than RoDynRF and DynNeRF?
questions.reference_answer: SplineGS runs at 400 FPS, RoDynRF at 0.45 FPS, and DynNeRF at 0.05 FPS. Therefore SplineGS is about 889x faster than RoDynRF and 8,000x faster than DynNeRF.

evidence.supports: FPS values: 400, 0.45, and 0.05.

questions.question: For novel view-and-time synthesis on NVIDIA, how much better is SplineGS than the best baseline in PSNR, LPIPS, and tOF?
questions.reference_answer: SplineGS reports 25.92 PSNR, 0.098 LPIPS, and 0.703 tOF. Among the listed baselines, DynNeRF is the strongest on all three metrics with 23.36 PSNR, 0.219 LPIPS, and 0.921 tOF. SplineGS improves PSNR by 2.56 dB, reduces LPIPS by 0.121, and reduces tOF by 0.218.

evidence.supports: Novel view-and-time metrics for SplineGS and baselines.

questions.question: In the SplineGS trajectory-model ablation, how does MAS compare with the Bezier baseline in quality and deformation latency?
questions.reference_answer: MAS gives 27.21 PSNR, 0.053 LPIPS, and 5.63 ns deformation latency per Gaussian, while Bezier gives 27.19 PSNR, 0.060 LPIPS, and 8.78 ns. MAS is 0.02 dB higher in PSNR, 0.007 lower in LPIPS, and about 35.9% lower in deformation latency.

evidence.supports: Bezier and MAS quality/latency rows.

questions.question: What benefit does MACP provide over using a fixed four control points for every dynamic Gaussian?
questions.reference_answer: With MACP, SplineGS obtains 27.21 PSNR, 0.053 LPIPS, and 5.63 ns deformation latency, compared with 26.62 PSNR, 0.065 LPIPS, and 5.34 ns for fixed Nc = 4. MACP improves PSNR by 0.59 dB and LPIPS by 0.012 at a small latency increase of 0.29 ns per Gaussian.

evidence.supports: Fixed Nc=4 versus full MACP model.

questions.question: Which SplineGS loss ablation is most catastrophic, and what are the numerical changes relative to the full model?
questions.reference_answer: Removing photometric-consistency loss L_pc is the most catastrophic ablation. PSNR falls from 27.21 to 17.49, a decrease of 9.72 dB, while LPIPS increases from 0.053 to 0.853, a degradation of 0.800.

evidence.supports: Loss-function ablation.

questions.question: What inference speed does Shape of Motion report on a smartphone or other mobile device?
questions.reference_answer: The paper does not report inference or rendering speed on a smartphone or mobile device. It reports GPU-side rendering/runtime information, but no mobile-device benchmark.

evidence.supports: GPU-side rendering/runtime information is reported here.

questions.negative_evidence_note: Absence of a mobile benchmark is a document-level negative claim. Do not score retrieval solely by finding one runtime sentence; score whether the agent avoids inventing a mobile result.

questions.question: MoSca relies on COLMAP to estimate camera poses before reconstruction. Which part of COLMAP does it use?
questions.reference_answer: The premise is incorrect. MoSca is designed to avoid requiring an external pose estimator such as COLMAP. It estimates focal length and camera poses using its own tracklet-based bundle adjustment and photometric optimization.

evidence.supports: Camera focal length and poses can be solved with bundle adjustment without other pose-estimation tools.
Explicitly states that the method obviates pose estimators such as COLMAP.

questions.question: SplineGS states that official MoSca code was unavailable when its Table 1 was prepared. Is that still true today?

evidence.supports: At paper time, the caption states that MoSca official code was unavailable.
